messages:
alice: quick question — we're adding an opt-out for client metrics in the python sdk. how should we expose it without breaking tracing or user-agent reporting?

ben: two quick goals: 1) keep User-Agent intact for telemetry/ops, 2) let customers completely disable sending metric pings (host-level) and per-request.

carol: +1. We have three knobs in the design doc: env var, client config bool, and per-request header override. Which one are you wiring?

alice: planning to add all three. env var REDWOOD_DISABLE_CLIENT_METRICS, client arg metrics_enabled=True, and header x-redwood-disable-metrics=1 for per-request. any objections?

ben: sounds fine. important: tracing propagation should remain default ON and use W3C headers (traceparent/tracestate). disabling metrics shouldn't stop injecting trace headers.

dmitri: agree. also note streaming requests (event/streaming endpoints) are tricky: they open a long-lived connection so metrics-flush behavior differs. we should skip metrics initialization in the streaming path if disabled.

alice: good call. for the python SDK implementation i'm thinking:
```py
class RedwoodClient:
    def __init__(self, api_key, metrics_enabled=True):
        self.metrics_enabled = metrics_enabled and os.getenv('REDWOOD_DISABLE_CLIENT_METRICS') != '1'

    def generate(self, *args, headers=None, metrics_override=None):
        headers = headers or {}
        if metrics_override is not None:
            headers['x-redwood-disable-metrics'] = '1' if not metrics_override else '0'
        else:
            if not self.metrics_enabled:
                headers['x-redwood-disable-metrics'] = '1'
        # always inject tracing headers via opentelemetry (separate integration)
        return http.post(..., headers=headers, stream=False)
```

alice: does that pattern seem ok?

carol: small nit: don't use header value 0/1 strings inconsistently. prefer explicit 'true'/'false' or 'disabled' to be human readable. also document precedence: per-request header > client config > env var.

ben: +1 on precedence and readable values. also add a clear note: user-agent should always be included unless customer sets a custom UA. SDK should append to any existing UA rather than replace. e.g., 'MyApp/1.2.3 RedwoodSDK-Py/1.12.3'

dmitri: regarding tracing — if customers use their own OTLP/OTEL setup, the SDK should not create a new span for a simple single-request wrapper. It should only inject context. For auto-instrumentation we need a separate integration doc.

alice: ok i'll update the PR to: use 'true'/'false' header values, implement precedence, and ensure traceparent/tracestate are injected via our existing opentelemetry helper. also special-case streaming: skip metrics client init if disabled and ensure we don't add metric flush hooks on stream abort.

carol: for retries: if metrics are disabled but you still want retry counts for billing/ops, we shouldn't re-enable metrics just for retries. retries should be observable by server-side logs; client-side toggles are purely client-controlled. mention that in docs.

ben: FYI deploy-bot: 1.12.3 to staging includes a metrics toggle flag (env + client config) — please watch staging traces/headers.

deploy-bot: release 1.12.3 deployed to staging at 2026-02-21T14:18:02Z — includes REDWOOD_DISABLE_CLIENT_METRICS support and header x-redwood-disable-metrics.

alice: thanks — i'll push the PR with tests for: header precedence, UA append behavior, and streaming path no-op when disabled. ping me for reviews.

dmitri: quick test idea: run a small OTEL collector locally and confirm traceparent is present whether metrics enabled or not. i can help write that test harness.

alice: awesome — will take that. anyone opposed to the header name staying as x-redwood-disable-metrics?

carol: fine with it, add it to the public SDK header docs and a migration note.

ben: one more: add a short blurb in CHANGELOG about telemetry opt-out and how it affects support (we may not see client-side metrics if disabled).

alice: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
